questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As I am studying a language, it felt very natural and as a opportunity I couldn't miss, to explore the language and the culture even more trough exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was definitely a bit difficult and stressful at times. You defiantly need to prioritize time and effort to do these things, and can expect information to come to you without searching for quite a while, that was my experience at least.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Contact details in form of email adresses, and opportunity to ask question at the introduction day

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Difficult, I will reccomend start looking in advance

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I got to experience the culture of the city this way, and enjoyed coming to the campus as a contrast, but glad I didn't live there full time

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A webportal

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Guides online and info at the introduction day

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was succesfull

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I used google a lot, to just search the courses i wanted, and then took it from there. And I used other Erasmus students, so we could help each other as we were all a little confused and in the same boat

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had to Erasmus courses with only international students in german, and two where I was the only exchange student in german as well. That was a good balance for me

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I didnt experience the biggest difference, as my courses at UCHPH also are in german. But there was some different ways of participating that i hadn't tried before. Making a "response paper" and a "protocol" was something i hadn't tried before as examples.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Film der Weimarer Republik
- Migration und Religion 
- Hedwig Dohm im Kontext der Frauenbewegung 
- Kreuzberg als Topos und Schauplatz in der Gegenwartsliteratur

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: For me it made a lot of sense to do courses that i could imagine being a potential theme for my bachelorprojekt. I tried to choose as many culture and literature courses, because that's where my interest is. I didn't choose anything based on social presences, but only academic interests.

questions.answer: A deposit for my apartment

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It was cheaper to live than i thought, the most expensive thing was housing

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Museums, sports-clubs, political groups

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was really happy to participate in the political and activist life both on and off campus

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Enjoy all the free cultural opportunities. There are so many. Lakes, parks and other outside offers are great as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it natural and easy, but took a little time of adjustment of course

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language of course, and a general lack of interest from the german students. But among exchange students, I found everyone to be open

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The culture around music, the history that is everywhere in the city, the diversity in the city

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1: School is important, but you can learn so much from exploring the city as well, find a balance and trust it! 2: Be brave and talk to new people (the entire stay), so many people are desperate for a friend, so you are all in the same boat. 3: Take pictures!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can actually find a lot of information by just googling it, if the website is difficult to navigate. And use the mensa, will save you so much money

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The connections and friends I made has changed me fundamentally as a person

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Coming home, I find it very underwhelming to come home with so many new experiences in the bag. I wish i could have stayed, but at least I know now that is could be a possibility for me to come back and live there one day

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
